articles.title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion makeover hit with another fresh roadblock despite $7,500 repair effort
articles.summary: Travis Kelce’s plans to turn his $5.35 million Ohio property into a private retreat have run into another roadblock.
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s plans to turn his $5.35 million Ohio property into a private retreat have run into another roadblock. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end has already spent money addressing concerns raised by nearby residents, but his efforts have not ended the dispute. What began as disagreements over fencing and privacy has now grown into a bigger debate about property damage, ageing infrastructure and the impact of luxury landscaping on a quiet lakeside community. The latest objections could force another change to the estate’s development plans.Travis Kelce’s mansion landscaping plans face fresh sewer concernsThe dispute centres on Kelce’s 21,000-square-foot estate in Bratenahl, Ohio, where neighbours have raised concerns about proposed landscaping near an old clay sewer line. One resident, Katherine Bolton, who has lived beside the property for 35 years, fears that planting around 50 evergreen trees could put the ageing pipeline at risk.Her concerns are not simply about appearances. Tree roots can enter existing cracks in underground pipes, gradually widening the damage and potentially causing expensive blockages or sewage problems. Bolton said she had received an estimate of $75,000 to line her sewer pipe.“Planting 50 evergreen trees just ten feet from a 100-year-old clay sewer line is virtually guaranteed to cause severe root intrusion, pipe structural failure, and catastrophic sewage backups,” she said, citing AI-based research.Another neighbour, Chuck Bauernschmidt, also questioned the changes to the property's surroundings. He presented photographs and alleged that much of the existing shrubbery had been removed. He further warned that the proposed spear-topped fence could injure deer moving through the neighbourhood.These objections have added another layer to a project that has already faced resistance over its six-foot security fence.Travis Kelce’s team spends $7,500 to address neighbours’ complaintsKelce's representatives have pushed back against suggestions that they have ignored the community's concerns. Jacob Kutz of Tiny Construction, who oversees the project, told the board that the property owners had already paid to repair part of the damaged sewer line.“without asking for any help, just to show we’re good neighbors.”The $7,500 repair was presented as evidence that the project team was willing to address problems rather than leave residents dealing with the consequences.The team also made several changes to the fence proposal. It was moved two feet inside the property's boundary, additional gates were included to preserve neighbours' access to the sewer line, and the plan to extend the fence towards the water was dropped.However, the latest hearing did not deliver everything Kelce's team wanted. Officials approved landscaping at the front of the estate, subject to conditions on tree spacing, but withheld approval for shoreline saplings because of concerns about their eventual height.The couple will now have to submit another revised proposal. For Kelce, the challenge is no longer just creating a secure and attractive home. It is finding a plan that satisfies local rules without creating further friction with the people living nearby.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: How Patrick Mahomes’ first Kansas City mansion went from a $1.9M purchase to a $2.9M listing before finding a buyer in under two weeks
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes has enjoyed plenty of big wins on the football field, but one of his early real estate moves also proved rewarding.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes has enjoyed plenty of big wins on the football field, but one of his early real estate moves also proved rewarding. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback bought his first home for $1.9 million in 2019, then put it on the market four years later for $2.9 million. The property found a buyer in less than two weeks, marking a quick end to a memorable chapter in his life. From a dedicated sneaker room to a backyard built for relaxation, the house reflected the lifestyle Mahomes was creating as his NFL career took off.Patrick Mahomes’ $1.9M Kansas City home featured luxury upgradesMahomes purchased the property in February 2019, shortly after winning the NFL's Most Valuable Player award for his remarkable 2018 season. Located at 1257 W. 57th St. in Kansas City's Sunset Hill neighbourhood, the ranch-style house was built in 1953 and sits on approximately 1.4 acres.At the time, Mahomes was still building his life with his then-girlfriend, Brittany Matthews, who later became his wife. The couple invested nearly $400,000 in renovations to transform the property into their first shared home.“This is the first house either of us ever owned,” the quarterback said during a video walkthrough of the renovation work.The home featured an open-plan design, offering plenty of space for everyday living. One room had a particularly personal purpose. It housed Mahomes' sneaker collection, which reportedly reached around 180 pairs at one point.The outdoor space was equally impressive. A heated swimming pool, hot tub and putting green gave the property a resort-like feel. The garage could also accommodate five vehicles, adding another attraction for potential buyers.Patrick Mahomes sells Kansas City mansion after listing it for $2.9MIn June 2023, Mahomes and his family decided to sell the Sunset Hill property. They listed it for $2.9 million, exactly $1 million above the original purchase price.The listing was handled by Cami Jones of ReeceNichols, who highlighted its location and traditional design.“Right off of Country Club Plaza, this stunning ranch style home is in the sought after subdivision of Sunset Hill.”The property attracted a buyer in less than two weeks. A trust connected to Kansas City businessman David “Rall” Bradley III purchased the house in late June. Bradley co-owns BERKS Group, a private equity firm, while his family also operates News-Press & Gazette Co.However, the final selling price was not disclosed, so the actual profit from the transaction remains unknown.Mahomes had already expanded his property portfolio before the sale, purchasing a $3.37 million home in Westlake, Texas, in March 2020. In 2023, the family moved into a much larger estate in Cass County, Missouri.His current mansion features a private football field and a par-3 golf hole, offering a glimpse of how much his lifestyle has evolved since buying his first home.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Travis Kelce’s $200 million investment faces high risk as Six Flags investigated for securities fraud amid tragic deaths
articles.summary: Travis Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs popular tight end, has been facing a tough time on the field as his team continues to suffer after losing in two
articles.body: Travis Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs popular tight end, has been facing a tough time on the field as his team continues to suffer after losing in two matches consecutively since last week. While this has sparked panic, it seems Travis Kelce’s $200 million investment in the popular amusement park, Six Flags, is headed for more trouble.Travis Kelce’s investment at risk as Six Flags Entertainment faces questioning over securities fraudAs per reports, law firm Bleichmar Fonti & Auld LLP is investigating Six Flags Entertainment for potential securities fraud related to its statements on safety and ride maintenance.This update comes after there was a tragic death at Six Flags Georgia after a 42 year old schoolteacher from Atlanta was ejected from his seat on the infamous Goliath roller coaster and fell to his death.The investigation done by the law firm is primarily focusing on if Six Flags Entertainment has misled its investors about the safety practices it has across their parks in the country.The law firm Bleichmar Fonti & Auld LLP is also actively seeking for investors to come forward with their complaints about their investment in Six Flags Entertainment.At this point in time, the tragic death at Six Flags Georgia has led to the temporary shut down of the infamous rollercoaster Goliath across 10 parks in the country while its stock witnessed a 14.4% drop in Six Flags' stock in October.The popular amusement park Six Flags Entertainment has not issued a statement about it yet while Travis Kelce has also remained silent.For the unversed, Travis Kelce’s name has been linked to Six Flags Investment ever since he teamed up with activist hedge fund JANA Partners for a $200 million investment in October 2025.The popular tight end has also become the amusement park’s brand ambassador and is often spotted promoting their sales.Travis Kelce has been linked to Six Flags Entertainment for over a year nowIn a social media post last year, Travis Kelce reflected on joining Six Flags as he wrote, “To all my fellow theme park and amusement park lovers. I have some exciting news!!!”The popular tight end added, “Couldn’t pass up the opportunity to continue the tradition and make Cedar Point and Six Flags even more special for the next generation of families! Excited to partner with JANA Partners as an investor in Six Flags. So crazy to even imagine this is real, but you gotta love it when life comes full circle.”Travis Kelce continued, “The chance to help make Six Flags special for the next generation is one I couldn’t pass up…”But he has maintained distance from the Six Flags Entertainment’s legal mess as he remains focused on his career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Patrick Mahomes’ wife Brittany Mahomes makes an emotional update about their family as the Chiefs face another setback
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ popular quarterback, is dealing with the controversial call at the game against the Denver Broncos which led to
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ popular quarterback, is dealing with the controversial call at the game against the Denver Broncos which led to the team’s second loss in a week, sparking concern about the team’s performance. While Patrick Mahomes’ wife, popular investor Brittany Mahomes, has been a strong source of support to him, she has made a few emotional confessions about her life.Patrick Mahomes’ wife, Brittany Mahomes, makes a few emotional comments as the Kansas City Chiefs deals with tough losses on the fieldJust a few hours ago, Patrick Mahomes’ wife, Brittany Mahomes, took to her social media to make a post that read as, “Sometimes I just look at my kids and think, how did I get so lucky that I actually made my favorite people in the entire world? Like, I grew these little humans and now I get to spend my life loving them. Nothing will ever beat that.”A second post made by Patrick Mahomes’ wife, Brittany Mahomes, read as, “Not sure who needs to hear this today, but... I pray that God, the source of hope, will fill you completely with joy and peace because you trust in him. Then you will overflow with confident hope through the power of the Holy Spirit. Romans 15:13.”Patrick Mahomes’ wife Brittany Mahomes posts come at a time when the star quarterback is dealing with a tough time on the field amid the controversial loss against the Denver Broncos.Patrick Mahomes remain emotional about the brutal loss against the Denver BroncosFor the unversed, Patrick Mahomes recorded a 73 yard touchdown pass to rookie running back Emmett Johnson to help give the Chiefs a halftime lead.He threw another 4 yard touchdown pass to tight end Noah Gray in the third quarter, putting the Chiefs up by 11 points.But things came crashing down at the end of the game when the Kansas City Chiefs were penalized 11 times for 105 yards during their 28-24 loss to the Denver Broncos.While Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce have been emotional about the loss, the team’s head coach Andy Reid has now reflected on it.In an interview with reporters, the team’s head coach Andy Reid said, "So, every one is important; attention to detail is important," said Reid. "We've got to go back, and we've just got to make sure we refocus ourselves on making sure we're doing the right things fundamentally, start some practice, and put a concentrated eﬀort forward to that."Andy Reid added, "Oﬀensively, it really came down to that. You win the game if you don't have the penalty on the score there at the end, with very little time left on the clock."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Why does Jerry Jones refuse to spend big on a head coach? Dallas Cowboys owner fires back at critics amid Super Bowl drought
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones is facing fresh criticism over his decision to keep head coach Brian Schottenheimer on a relatively modest salary.
articles.body: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones is facing fresh criticism over his decision to keep head coach Brian Schottenheimer on a relatively modest salary. However, Jones does not believe spending more on a coach guarantees better results. During his latest appearance on 105.3 The Fan, he defended his hiring philosophy with a blunt message for those questioning his approach.The comments came as Dallas struggled through a 3-5 start to the 2026 NFL season. The Cowboys have not won a Super Bowl since the 1995 season, and supporters are growing impatient. Yet Jones remains convinced that finding the right coach matters more than offering the biggest contract.Jerry Jones has a blunt response to criticism over Cowboys coaching salariesDuring his interview on Dallas radio station 105.3 The Fan, Jones faced questions about his preference for finding less expensive coaching candidates who could develop into successful NFL head coaches.The Cowboys owner made his position clear."There is zero correlation [in the NFL] between how much you pay a coach or how many coaches you have as to winning. There is no correlation," Jones said during the radio appearance. "And that's a random sample of years and all 32 teams involved. So put that in your hopper and smoke it."His response came amid criticism over Schottenheimer's reported salary. Several reports have placed the Cowboys coach's annual earnings below those of the NFL's highest-paid head coaches. Estimates put Schottenheimer's salary at around $4.5 million, although exact coaching contracts remain difficult to verify because teams do not have to disclose their financial details.By comparison, some of the NFL's biggest coaching names earn between $14 million and $20 million annually.However, Jones has not always avoided hiring established coaches. In 2003, he brought Hall of Famer Bill Parcells out of retirement and gave him a four-year contract worth a reported $17.1 million.Parcells immediately improved Dallas. After the Cowboys finished 5-11 in 2002, he guided them to a playoff appearance in his first season. He remained with the franchise through the 2006 season but never took the team to a Super Bowl. Brian Schottenheimer's Cowboys struggles put Jerry Jones under pressureJones' latest comments have attracted more attention because Schottenheimer has yet to deliver the results Dallas wants.The Cowboys appointed Schottenheimer as head coach in January 2025 after he spent two seasons as their offensive coordinator. His first campaign ended with a 7-9-1 record. The offense averaged 27.7 points per game, but defensive problems repeatedly hurt the team's chances.The 2026 season has brought another difficult start. Dallas entered November with a 3-5 record after losing 33-30 to the Arizona Cardinals on November 1.The Cowboys appeared close to securing a much-needed victory, but Arizona fought back and forced overtime. Chad Ryland then converted a 42-yard field goal to hand the Cardinals the win.The defeat increased scrutiny around Schottenheimer and Jones' decision to appoint him. Dallas has also struggled to regain its playoff reputation. The franchise last won a postseason game in January 2024, when it lost 48-32 to Green Bay in the Wild Card Round.For Jones, the bigger challenge remains ending the franchise's Super Bowl drought. The Cowboys have not reached the championship game since the 1995 season.His argument that expensive coaches do not guarantee championships may hold some truth. But with Dallas struggling again, Schottenheimer needs to turn the season around. Otherwise, Jones' confidence in his lower-cost coaching approach will face even more criticism.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: “Chance at giving back and helping them”: How Justin Herbert is helping other kids experience the youth sports program that changed his life
articles.summary: Before Justin Herbert became the Los Angeles Chargers' franchise quarterback, he was a young athlete growing up in Eugene, Oregon.
articles.body: Before Justin Herbert became the Los Angeles Chargers' franchise quarterback, he was a young athlete growing up in Eugene, Oregon. He spent his childhood playing football, basketball, baseball and soccer through Kidsports. After many years, Herbert returned to support the organisation that gave him those opportunities. Through his charity golf invitational, he wants to make sure money does not stop other children from enjoying the same experience.His connection with Kidsports goes beyond a fundraising appearance. Herbert has made the organisation's work part of his efforts to give back to his hometown, helping local families afford youth sports and giving children a chance to build friendships through competition. How Justin Herbert turned his childhood experience with Kidsports into a missionHerbert first took steps to support Kidsports in 2021, when he announced the Justin Herbert Invitational at Shadow Hills Country Club. The inaugural tournament took place on July 8, 2021, with a fundraising target of $100,000. The event also brought together football personalities and local businesses, with the money going towards helping children participate in sports.Speaking to KMTR on April 9, 2021, Herbert explained why he wanted to bring the fundraiser to Eugene."Eugene's always been my home and I've loved that community and they've given me so much. If I have even the slightest chance at giving back and helping them, I'd love to do it," he said.His connection with the organisation was deeply personal. During a KMTR interview on July 8, 2021, he spoke about the opportunities he received as a child."Having gone through it for so many years, I know how great it is," Herbert said.He also explained how those experiences shaped him beyond sports."I think so much is learned through sports, stuff that you don't learn in the classroom," the Chargers quarterback said during the July 8 interview. "Teamwork and commitment and - just to have fun, and growing up and playing with your best friends, I don't think it gets much better than that."Herbert also made his intentions clear when discussing the money raised through the invitational."All of the money, all of the proceeds will go to making sure that every kid will have a chance to play," he told KMTR in its April 9, 2021 report.Justin Herbert returned in 2022 as Kidsports continued helping thousands of childrenThe fundraiser did not end with its inaugural edition. On July 7, 2022, Herbert returned to Eugene for the second annual Justin Herbert Invitational at Shadow Hills Country Club. The event continued supporting Kidsports and its efforts to make youth sports accessible to local families.During KMTR's July 7, 2022 report, executive director Bev Smith revealed that Kidsports had never turned a child away in her 12 years with the organisation. She explained that it provided scholarship assistance to around 4,000 children annually and raised approximately $250,000 each year to fund the programme.The money also helped the organisation bring free sports camps directly into local communities, so children from families with limited resources did not have to travel to participate.Herbert also remembered his own early football experiences during the 2022 event. He recalled winning flag football championships with his friends, including games played at Churchill High School.The quarterback admitted he never expected to reach the NFL when he was playing for Sheldon High School."No chance! I thought high school football was the biggest deal in the world and just playing for Sheldon, playing quarterback on the varsity team, that meant the world to me and I thought that was it," Herbert told KMTR on July 7, 2022.He also spoke about learning to handle setbacks through sports."I know you learn about losing and dealing with adversity and I think that's helped me off better in the long run," Herbert said during the same interview.From those childhood games in Eugene to becoming an NFL quarterback, Herbert has carried those lessons with him. His annual golf invitational gives him a way to support the organisation that helped shape those early years and help other children get their own chance to play.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Buyers, sellers or fence-sitters? All 32 NFL teams slotted before the trade deadline
articles.summary: We sorted all 32 teams into three categories ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline: buyers, sellers and fence-sitters.
articles.body:
NFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | Commanders NFC North : Bears | Lions | Packers | Vikings NFC South: Falcons | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers NFC West: Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | Seahawks

AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots | Jets AFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns | Steelers AFC South: Texans | Colts | Jaguars | Titans AFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | Chargers

Where does your team sit as the NFL's trade deadline fast approaches?

Not all needy teams will swing trades prior to Nov. 10, but some certainly will look. On the other end of the spectrum, not all out-of-contention teams will hold fire sales, but with the recent spate of big names moving, there are opportunities to sell now and cash in later.

And, as we know, some teams will sit idly by as the deadline comes and goes. The NFL might be as active, trade-wise, as it has ever been in-season, but not every team is willing to pay the asking prices they're hearing.

Here's how we view all 32 teams, slotting each of them into one of three categories — buyers, fence-sitters and sellers — prior to the trade deadline. Teams are roughly ordered within each section by their perceived fits: strongest at the top, weakest at the bottom.

The Bills are the top seed in the AFC in spite of a defense that clearly needs help. Sunday's blowout of the Ravens notwithstanding, that unit isn't as likely to perform to that level against top-tiered quarterbacks and offenses. There are questions about how much the Bills want to give up in any prospective trade, and they're hamstrung a bit right now by salary-cap space (less than $4 million), but that can be rectified if needed. Safety might be the biggest position of need, although they also could look for extra pass-rush help.

Defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton suffered a torn quadriceps in Sunday's win over the Colts and will miss the rest of the season. It's hard to understate how big a blow this is. Head coach Liam Coen said the Jags will take a committee approach to replacing Hamilton, but finding a nose tackle is easier than finding other positions, so it would not be surprising to see them try to add a plugger up front. Safety is another spot they could consider. The Jaguars (5-2) are steamrolling toward a division title, and are in the hunt for the AFC's top seed. There's no better time to go for it.

They're already buyers after the DeForest Buckner trade , and they might not be done. They reportedly reached out to the Vikings about Jauan Jennings before they found out Jennings wasn't interested in a return. But receiver figures to be a position they consider upgrading, along with edge rusher and possibly cornerback. The 49ers have to be very cautious with Mike Evans; they've been a vastly better team with him on the field. Adding WR insurance, given all the injuries there, feels like a low-risk move that's on the table.

Their first buy of trade season, Jeffery Simmons, sunk his teeth into the Seahawks on Monday night . It's the kind of move that turned a very good team into a downright scary one. You can't blame the Bears if that's all general manager Ryan Poles gets done prior to the deadline, but the one area of concern coming out of the Seattle game had to be cornerback. Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson both had rough nights with Malik Muhammad out, so we expect Poles to work the phones for CB help. They also could look for a pass-rush addition, with old friend Khalil Mack a name often bandied about these days. The Bears appear to be in Super Bowl mode now. They're out shopping.

The Vikings' offense could keep them from a Super Bowl, so they figure to seek help on that side of the ball — specifically a running back or an offensive guard. The run game has slowed down, and Aaron Jones Sr. has battled knee issues. The Vikings really could use more of a workhorse to complement Jones and Jordan Mason. They've also been connected to some pass rushers, scary as that sounds for opponents.

The Chiefs are stricken by limited salary cap space, but they figure to look and see what's out there. Wide receiver is the biggest area of concern — again — with Tyquan Thornton out for the season and Rashee Rice seemingly dealing with chronic soft-tissue issues. General manager Brett Veach has a decent history of smaller-to-medium deadline moves, so you can't rule anything out here. They also could mine for pass-rush help, but that might be tougher to find — and afford.

The primary need appears to be on defense, a unit that started strong but has tailed off. The Bengals could use help at multiple spots, although cornerback figures to be the most concerning, especially after watching Cam Ward pick them apart Sunday. A coverage linebacker and another pass rusher would be nice, too. On offense, if there's a need, it's at running back. They're averaging 3.7 yards per rush, with a long run of 15 yards this season.

Dallas is 3-5 yet still in the hunt for how poor the NFC East is. Team owner Jerry Jones says the Cowboys remain on the lookout for more help, and though they had been historically quiet at the trade deadline, Jones backed up his talk with last year's deadline deal for Quinnen Williams and the earlier-season trade for Joey Porter Jr. The Cowboys' defense is getting manhandled now . They badly need pass-rush help, but another corner would also be nice. Then again, so could more LB help. Jones said they won't want to flush more draft picks on a player who isn't under contract long term, but they might be desperate enough to add wherever they can.

The Patriots remain in contention at 5-3 (and a 3-0 mark in the division), but they could have concerns on both sides of the ball. On offense, they could use guard reinforcements after Alijah Vera-Tucker and Mike Onwenu landed on injured reserve. On defense, pass-rush help probably tops the list, but they also could seek LB and DB depth. Following the major A.J. Brown trade this summer, it would be surprising if the Patriots relinquished major draft assets. Any moves they make figure to be on the lower-compensation side, perhaps for a veteran's expiring contract.

Detroit fans have let general manager Brad Holmes know they want action prior to the deadline, especially after seeing the 49ers, Seahawks and Bears add starters last week. The Lions' defense is the biggest concern by far. The injuries to LBs Jack Campbell and Jimmy Rolder have left a big hole in the middle. Safety is in better shape with Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph back, but cornerback remains problematic. Pass-rush help also could be addressed. Can Holmes find the right help in the next week?

After adding Rashid Shaheed last year and Quenton Nelson this year, we know the Seahawks are open for business this time of year. Did Monday's home blowout loss to the Bears change their level of aggression? A struggling run game is an area the Seahawks could seek to help, although Zach Charbonnet's return could make them look elsewhere. They could try to add one more pass rusher and possibly another receiver for an offense that has been too JSN-dependent.

The Giants have found themselves atop the NFC East, and their first in-season trade for QB J.J. McCarthy has borne some early fruit. Could that move portend another (or others) if the Giants keep finding ways to win? Possibly. We know that John Harbaugh personally called Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk about Jeffery Simmons, but that call went to voicemail and Simmons went to Chicago. Defensive tackle figures to be the spot most likely to be addressed, but don't rule out a cheaper running back to stabilize that shakier position.

The Steelers already have been sellers, trading CB Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys. But sitting in first place in the AFC North in what's roundly expected to be Aaron Rodgers' final season, the Steelers might try to get back to buying. Not coincidentally, they could use a cornerback. Safety and wide receiver also could be spots they seek to upgrade. This doesn't feel like a team, however, that's prepared to go broke for that proverbial one final move.

They were close to being labeled "fence-sitters" after Sunday's breakout from RB Jonah Coleman. Running back had been the position that seemed most in need of being addressed prior to Coleman's big game Sunday. Now that feels like a luxury. Their most likely target position, if they try to swing a deal, figures to be offensive line or tight end.

This felt like an all-in season at one point, but that was before Myles Garrett and Davante Adams got hurt and the team started 2-4. The Rams have since evened their record at .500, but several tough games remain. The Rams certainly could be active, and another receiver certainly would help, but they've already depleted their trade assets significantly with the Garrett deal and don't have a ton to give up. They might want to add some help, but can the Rams realistically make an impact trade in time? It's unclear.

They've had some recent tailwind as a team, they've gotten Josh Jacobs back and Micah Parsons' return appears to be on the horizon. They also have some possible needs, including cornerback, if they can find the right trade partner. On the other hand, they've just been so historically quiet around the deadline under GM Brian Gutekunst (they actually have been more deadline sellers than anything), that I wonder if they'll do much.

The Texans have already bought, adding WR Marvin Harrison Jr., but is more coming? There are questions in the offensive and defensive backfields, and they continue to struggle to get the offensive line fully right. All those spots are possible. But the Texans are 2-5 and falling farther behind the first-place Jaguars. If Houston makes a move, expect it to be more on the minor end.

How seriously are the Browns taking their 5-3 start, especially after the humbling loss to first-place Pittsburgh? There are plenty of areas they could address, ample draft assets to part with and a general manager in Andrew Berry who has been among the most active in-season traders. But if the Browns don't feel this team has a legitimate chance to make playoff noise, they might be wise to keep their assets and load up more in the offseason. Browns fans would be giddy at a deadline deal, but patience might be preferred.

The Raiders feel like they are in no-man's land. They pulled back to .500 after losing four straight, but is Vegas capable of contending? The big drama now feels like when the Raiders will move off of Kirk Cousins and give the reins to Fernando Mendoza. There might be a case for the Raiders as sellers, with Cousins perhaps an intriguing piece for a team such as the Ravens that recently lost its starting QB. Other possible trade figures include Jackson Powers-Johnson and Adam Butler, but it also feels like the Raiders could ride things out without any major transactions the rest of the way.

The Panthers are a strange team to handicap. Carolina has clear needs, but at 3-4, with two straight losses, is it in position to add help? Oh, and did we mention that record puts the Panthers in first place? The playoffs are still very much a possibility, but this team being one or two moves away from being a Super Bowl contender is a stretch. If the Panthers add somewhere, cornerback feels like the most likely spot. Anything they do likely would have to be more than just a short-term rental at retail price.

Most of the NFC South profiles similarly to Carolina. There's a real shot at winning the division, but at what cost? There's also the chance the Bucs could look to sell, with names such as Yaya Diaby, A'Shawn Robinson and Chris Godwin Jr. being floated. But GM Jason Licht has not made an in-season trade since Tom Brady was QB, and it feels like the chances are greater that the Bucs do nothing.

They're 3-5 and 1-2 in the division, yet Atlanta has enough explosive potential offensively to be potential buyers. Even after Michael Penix Jr.'s four-INT game, the Falcons might think they have a real shot of taking the division. The receiver depth is light, and there are still holes to patch on defense, although they might treat the return of James Pearce Jr. from suspension as their big pre-deadline addition.

I'd put the Saints more in the "sellers" bin, sitting at 2-5 with team owner Gayle Benson already having aired her grievances with the team's performance publicly. A loss to the Browns this weekend might push them closer to moving some pieces. The question is about what players might be available and sought by other teams. If another team wanted Alvin Kamara or Cameron Jordan, the Saints would almost have to sell. Otherwise, there just aren't a lot of tradable assets that might tempt other teams.

The Jets certainly could be sellers, with the season again slipping away and the focus continuing to shift to what could be one of the franchise's biggest offseasons, armed with three first-round draft picks — with all three currently in the top 10. Adding to that should be a consideration. Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall are two big names that could be on the move, but to this point they've publicly pushed back against dealing either. If they are active, I expect lower-profile pieces such as Harrison Phillips or Nahshon Wright to be more likely than the bigger names.

The Commanders kept their season alive in the watered-down NFC East with a win over the Eagles on Sunday night, and there's a chance they could be lighter buyers if they can find a running back who fits their short- and long-term vision. They also could be sellers, with pass rusher K'Lavon Chaisson the most logical piece to try to move. It's hard to get a clear read on what GM Adam Peters wants to do, but he said he's talked to all 31 teams and continues to work the phones.

The Colts have already sold off two major assets in Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner. There's not much stopping them from continuing to put other players up for sale. WR Josh Downs has reportedly requested a trade and figures to be in play in the coming days. RB Jonathan Taylor might cost too much to be moved before the deadline, but the Colts are acting like a team just waiting for a bigger offer to pull the trigger. Lacking a first-round pick in 2027, the Colts need all the draft-pick help they can get.

For years, GM Howie Roseman has been about the most aggressive talent hunter out there come deadline time. This season, following a string of poor developments and six straight losses, the Eagles look far more like sellers on the outside. There is no shortage of players the Eagles could move. They have several expiring-contract candidates, including TE Dallas Goedert, CB Riq Woolen, WR Marquise Brown, DT Moro Ojomo and others. There also are players under contract beyond 2026 who could be available, including OG Landon Dickerson and Edge Nolan Smith. They've already made one trade and could be open for more business with this season apparently shot.

The Chargers have continued to hoard assets for now, but as the league's final winless team, it's worth wondering what they're waiting for. GM Joe Hortiz was turning away calls at one point because the team believed a turnaround was coming. It was not. If they finally become sellers, Khalil Mack figures to be an easy piece to move — a veteran pass rusher on an expiring deal. Teams seeking nose tackle help should probably call on Dalvin Tomlinson. WR Quentin Johnston also could be available if the team doesn't think he can reach his ceiling there. There are deals to be made if the Chargers shift their thinking.

The Dolphins are not making the playoffs this year, although it's reasonable to be encouraged by their competitiveness. Still, this is a sell-off phase for the Dolphins if they can cook up some interest in players such as Zach Sieler, Austin Jackson, Josh Uche or others. The problem is that Miami's roster is already so heavily loaded with rookies and minimum-salary players that there are only so many assets to move. But the Dolphins gladly will vacuum up any draft picks other teams are willing to fork over in this multiyear rebuild.

Shipping out well-liked Jeffery Simmons was a sign that the Titans are in sell-now mode. RB Tony Pollard is probably their most tradable piece, but it's not clear if they want to move him. Anyone can have WR Calvin Ridley for a song, if they want. Edge Jermaine Johnson II also might be a name you hear this week after picking him up from the Jets this offseason. This might not be a fire sale, per se, but they're apparently open for business.

Even after Sunday's dramatic win in Dallas, the Cardinals feel more like sellers than buyers, having already shipped out Marvin Harrison Jr. and sitting at fourth place in one of the toughest divisions. If a QB-needy team wants Jacoby Brissett, the team shouldn't hesitate trading him, especially after benching him for Gardner Minshew in the dramatic comeback. Pass rusher Josh Sweat feels like the biggest player who most reasonably could be moved now, although Budda Baker's name has also come up. They have some assets that could be moved, but will the Cardinals act on that?

In a single moment, when Lamar Jackson suffered his thumb injury against the Bills, the Ravens might have gone from buyers to sellers. The one exception might be at QB, where the Ravens could opt to swing a trade, be it for someone like Kirk Cousins or perhaps Bears backup Tyson Bagent, who played last year with Ravens OC Declan Doyle. But if the Ravens lose Thursday, they might consider moving a few players, including Marlon Humphrey, Mark Andrews and Roquan Smith.

articles.title: ‘I Really Hope He Doesn’t Get Fined For This’ — Packers Fans Beyond Amused as Jordan Love And His Wife Troll NFL Refs After Lions Controversy
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love and his wife, Ronika Stone Love, found a hilarious way to express their frustration with NFL officiating this Hallo...
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love and his wife, Ronika Stone Love, found a hilarious way to express their frustration with NFL officiating this Halloween. The couple's costume quickly went viral, with fans fully embracing their not-so-subtle dig at officials following Green Bay's controversial loss to the Detroit Lions in Week 7.

Love and Ronika dressed up as blind NFL referees, complete with the zebra-striped shirts, dark sunglasses, and white canes.

Jordan Love and His Wife's Halloween Costumes Get Fans Talking

The joke went viral after Ronika posted a clip on TikTok captioned "I'm joking, I'm joking."

In the video , the couple can be seen blindly stumbling around, tapping their white canes, and launching yellow penalty flags into the air for no apparent reason.

Fans quickly filled the comments section, with many finding the joke hilarious while others worried the quarterback could face a fine from the NFL.

One fan joked, "You're gonna get us fined." Another supporter jokingly remarked, "Chill, Ronika, we play away this weekend, the refs might see this."

Others shared similar concerns, with one commenter saying, "I can smell the fine coming," while another added, "I really hope he doesn't get fined for this."

One fan even offered to cover the cost, saying , "I'll pay the fine"

Love's wife also joined the fun in the comments, responding to the growing attention with a simple message intended to cover all bases: "We're Footlocker employees."

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

The couple's costume was more than just a random Halloween gag, of course. It came after Green Bay suffered a frustrating 20-17 loss to the Detroit Lions in Week 7, with several officiating decisions becoming a major talking point.

Referee Alex Moore's crew called eight penalties against the Packers for 81 yards, with some decisions drawing criticism from fans and analysts.

The biggest talking point was the roughing-the-passer calls against defensive linemen Brenton Cox Jr. and Karl Brooks.

Brooks was flagged late in the fourth quarter after making contact with Jared Goff following an 18-yard completion. Tom Brady, in the FOX booth for the game, was clearly unhappy with the decision, saying, "That's definitely not roughing the passer!" Former NFL Vice President of Officiating Dean Blandino also backed Brady's criticism.

Other calls against defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt for unnecessary roughness and an intentional grounding penalty against Love added to Green Bay's frustration.

The controversy continued to attract attention even after the game ended. The NFL reassigned Moore and his crew from their scheduled primetime assignment for the Philadelphia Eagles vs. Washington Commanders game the following week.

articles.title: Vikings’ Carson Wentz Gets Good News on Promotion Before Bills Game
articles.summary: Minnesota Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz could be in line to start his second game of the season against the Buffalo Bills on MNF. The post Vikings’ Carson...
articles.body:
Calls among Minnesota Vikings fans and media members who cover the team regularly are steadily growing for Kevin O'Connell to make a change under center from Kyler Murray to Carson Wentz, and the head coach may have just caught the break he needed to do so while still allowing the franchise to save face.

The Vikings named Murray the starting QB over JJ McCarthy before either had taken a preseason snap. Minnesota then demoted McCarthy to QB3 before trading him to the New York Giants for a fifth-round draft asset in what was a fairly historic punt on top-10 pick in just his third NFL season at 23 years old and with only 10 starts on his resumé.

Murray has not performed poorly enough that one can accurately call his season through seven games a worst-case scenario for the Vikings. But across the range of possible outcomes, Murray has definitely produced on the lower end of the spectrum.

Benching him outright now would equate to O'Connell and first-year GM Nolan Teasley admitting that Murray's elevation to QB1 and the team's hastiness to sell low on McCarthy were both significant mistakes.

However, Murray's moderate hamstring concern, which he suffered in the team's first loss of the season last week to the Detroit Lions , might be precisely the window O'Connell requires to go back to Wentz while maintaining plausible deniability with regards to Murray.

Kyler Murray Suffered Hamstring Concern Last Week

O'Connell mentioned during the postgame that hamstring tightness was the reason for Murray's trip to the blue tent on the sidelines during the fourth quarter in Detroit.

On Tuesday, November 3, Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network reported that Murray could miss time due to the injury, which isn't overly severe but may impact his ability to scramble.

"I don't get the sense it's really bad, but he is a mobile QB," Rapoport said . "If he can't move like he needs to, then I don't know that he's gonna play."

Making plays with his legs has been Murray's saving grace this season, and if he can't do that effectively, it's hard to imagine the Vikings scoring enough points to keep up with the visiting Buffalo Bills on next week's addition of "Monday Night Football."

Vikings Arguably Soft-Benched JJ McCarthy for Carson Wentz Last Season

Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk wrote Tuesday that he suspects the Vikings will use Murray's injury as "cover" for a "soft benching" that will allow O'Connell to go back to Wentz without formally demoting Murray.

"It's hard not to look at the current status of Murray's hamstring 'tightness' as cover for a soft benching of Murray," Florio wrote . "That gives the Vikings a chance to let Carson Wentz, who played well enough in most of the Week 1 win over the Packers and all of the Week 2 win over the Bears ."

Several analysts suggested that Minnesota did essentially the same thing last season after McCarthy suffered a high ankle sprain in Week 2. Wentz stepped in, starting the next five games over a six-week span that included the Vikings' bye.

McCarthy eventually got the starting job back, though only after Wentz went down for the season with a shoulder injury that required surgery. If he had not suffered that injury when he did, circumstances would have forced the Vikings to tip their hand as to their true preferences at QB, with six weeks being the upward amount of time any player might legitimately miss with an ankle sprain — absent any setbacks.

articles.title: 2027 NFL Draft QB rankings: LaNorris Sellers is delivering on his talent
articles.summary: After a lot of movement early in the season in the 2027 NFL Draft QB rankings, things are starting to settle as the calendar turns to November. Drew Mestemak...
articles.body:
After a lot of movement early in the season in the 2027 NFL Draft QB rankings, things are starting to settle as the calendar turns to November.

Drew Mestemaker is the clear No. 1 QB in this class, even if he ends up going back to school for another year to gain some more experience. Dante Moore, after starting the season as a clear top-five pick, now is surrounded by questions as his college career was cut short. The same, of course, goes for Brendan Sorsby.

But there are still some very impressive signal-callers that are rising up the rankings. LaNorris Sellers , after starting the season by falling down the rankings, is now rising back up and playing some of the best football of his South Carolina career . Austin Simmons has been arguably the fastest riser of the season, and he continued that with another strong game on Saturday.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Week 10 is one of the biggest slates in recent memory in college football, and there will be plenty of chances for all of these guys to make big statements over the weekend. Heading into that lineup of juicy games, how do the top 10 QBs in the upcoming NFL Draft shake out?

Mestemaker got let down by his defense and a few bad decisions of his own on Saturday night, but he still finished with 323 yards and five touchdowns in a crazy 51-49 loss to Iowa State. That's kind of the story with Mestemaker week in and week out at this point. Mestemaker can make all the throws, he is a great athlete, and all of that is on display every time he takes the field. But his inexperience costs him in a big way once or twice throughout the game, and sometimes that's enough to cost the Cowboys and their defense the game.

After a rough day at the office against Texas, Chambliss got back on track on Saturday with a three-touchdown day against Auburn in a 45-15 win. It was nice to see the Rebels lean back into using Chambliss as a runner, as he gashed the Tigers on a number of designed runs and finished with 65 yards and a score on the ground. Now, a big test awaits. Chambliss will welcome Georgia back to Oxford after torching the Bulldogs twice last season, including in the Sugar Bowl to end their season. Kirby Smart's group will be very hungry, but that might not matter if the senior quarterback is on his game.

Sellers threw a pair of interceptions on Saturday, but it's hard not to be enamored with his physical tools as he continues to marry that with good process as a passer and improved accuracy. Sellers finished with nearly 400 yards of offense and five touchdowns on the road against a very good Oklahoma defense in a 42-25 win, including 96 yards and two scores as a runner. He is one of the most explosive athletes in this class, regardless of position, and the playmaking bag that unlocks was on full display in this game.

Sellers will have to end up in the right situation in the NFL, preferably with an offensive coordinator that will allow him to use his legs and unlock his talent as a playmaker. But if he does, the sky is the limit for him.

Mensah and the Miami offense had to bail out a shaky Hurricanes defense on Saturday night in a 38-35 win over North Carolina, and they did just that. The star quarterback finished 22-of-29 with 274 yards and three touchdowns, operating with the same precision, timing and accuracy that has him right in the middle of the Heisman Trophy discussion this season. Mensah also showed off his scrambling ability in this game, which he is capable of but doesn't like to use often. He finished with 36 yards on the ground, and Miami might need more where that came from if it is going to keep its undefeated season going with a win over Notre Dame.

The Missouri offense got off to a bit of a slow start on Saturday in a win over Arkansas, but Simmons' arm talent was on full display. he finished 20-of-31 with 179 yards and two touchdowns in what ended up as a 34-10 win, but it was his throw of the year candidate that caught the attention of scouts and fans alike online.

Simmons still has some inconsistencies in his game, but he is the real deal from the pocket. There will be plenty of NFL teams willing to take a chance on a player who is willing and able to access all of the throws, even in tight windows, with real velocity and ball placement on a consistent basis.

Carr and Notre Dame kicked it into gear when it mattered on Saturday despite a slow start against Navy, but that was more about the shortcomings of the defense than it was anything about Carr's performance. But rhetorical fact of the matter is that Carr hasn't been forced to be uncomfortable all that much this season, and the results were somewhat mixed in the Irish's loss to BYU. On Saturday, he will surely have to rise up and put the offense on his back at times against No. 1 Miami.

Manning and Texas finally were able to breeze through a game, as they dismantled a Mississippi State team whose season has been derailed by the injury to Kamario Taylor. Manning had a solid, but unspectacular, game, finishing 16-of-20 with 220 yards and three touchdowns. The junior QB's toughness and grit was on display, as he took a number of big hits but continued to lead the Longhorns offense up and down the field.

Now, Manning embarks on one of his toughest stretches of schedule yet. The Longhorns will go on the road to take on a Missouri team with a very good pass rush on Saturday, and then they will head to Death Valley for a date with LSU in Week 11. If he can excel against those two defenses, he could start to rise back up these rankings.

Moore will continue holding strong in this spot most likely, as there is a pretty steep tier gap between Manning at seven and Brendan Sorsby at nine. His career in college is very likely over, but Moore still has plenty of arm talent and a lot of good tape in 2025 that teams can go back to. His ability to play with pressure in his face will remain a question all the way up to the draft.

Sorsby is in a similar spot to Moore, as some quarterbacks have risen firmly above him while others have fallen far below. It seems unlikely that he will move far from this spot either way over the rest of the season. Of course, how he handles the pre-draft process and addresses his gambling scandal will be key in how high teams are willing to take him.

Minchey makes his debut in these rankings as one of the biggest risers of the season for Will Stein's resurgent Kentucky program. Minchey nearly beat out C.J. Carr for the starting job at Notre Dame before last season, and this year he is showing why he made that battle so competitive. He conducts the Kentucky offense very well and runs Stein's system almost perfectly. On top of that, Minchey is an effective playmaker who is additive to the explosiveness of the Kentucky attack as the Wildcats chase a CFP berth.

Next five: Jayden Maiava (USC), Drake Lindsey (Minnesota), Julian Sayin (Ohio State) C.J Bailey (NC State), Nico Iamaleava (UCLA)
